source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Heater and Air Conditioning, p.1A-37

procedures.title: Refrigerant leak at O-ring connection: repair
steps: (Continuing) discharge the system as in Evacuating and Charging Procedures.
Check the O-ring and fitting and replace either if damaged at all.
Coat the O-ring with clean refrigeration oil before refitting it, and fit it carefully.
Retighten the fitting using a backing wrench, put 1/2 to 1 lb. of R-12 in the system and leak test again.
Purge out that 1/2 to 1 lb. test charge.
notes: Caution: never run the system on the small test charge.

procedures.title: Refrigerant leak at hose clamp connection: repair
steps: Check the clamp is tight, tighten if needed and leak test again.
If it still leaks, discharge the system, loosen the clamp and pull the hose off.
Inspect hose and connector; replace any scored or damaged part.
Dip the end of the new hose in clean refrigeration oil and slide it carefully onto the connector, never past the locating bead.
Leak test with 1/2 to 1 lb. of R-12 in the system, without running the compressor.

procedures.title: Compressor leaks
steps: For leaks at the shaft seal or shell, replace the seals as covered under Compressor in the Chassis Overhaul Shop Manual.

procedures.title: Refrigerant hose failure
steps: After a hose leak or rupture, or a loose fitting that lost much refrigerant and oil, repair it, then flush and recharge the whole system.
If the system stood open to the atmosphere for a long time, also replace the receiver-dehydrator.
